_why: XbSymbolDatabase does not cover XMV, the video library, so these five
addresses had no names and could not be replaced by name.
They were found by scripts/section_calls.py, which reports the calls that
cross into a section from outside it: the XMV section spans
0x0023EB40..0x00266874 and the title reaches all of it through these five.
The names are the XDK's own, deduced from how the callers use each one --
Addresses are per title, not per XDK version: a statically linked library
lands wherever the linker put it. Only the behaviour is shared.

symbols.name: XMVPlaybackCreate
symbols._note: 0x0023EC4D. Third argument is the address of the caller's handle field; returns non-zero on failure, which makes the title call its error callback.

symbols.name: XMVPlaybackDestroy
symbols._note: 0x0023F191. The caller zeroes its handle field straight afterwards.

symbols.name: XMVPlaybackGetStreamInfo
symbols._note: 0x0023F275. Copies three fields out of the playback object at +0x40, +0x44 and +0x48 into the caller's struct at +0, +4 and +0xC.

symbols.name: XMVPlaybackStart
symbols._note: 0x0023F291. The caller sets its own playing flag afterwards.

symbols.name: XMVPlaybackUpdate
symbols._note: 0x0023F45C. Writes a status through its third argument: 0 keeps playing, 1 means finished and makes the title set its done flag, 2 and 3 are the paused or stopped states.
